title: California $800 franchise tax: Due dates and how to pay
summary: Find the California $800 tax deadline for your LLC or corporation, check first-year rules, and choose the right FTB payment type.
body_markdown:
California's $800 tax has different rules for LLCs and corporations. Start with your entity's **tax classification** , then identify the tax year and payment type. The deadline for paying the tax is not necessarily the deadline for filing the return.


For an LLC taxed as a partnership or disregarded entity, the annual tax generally applies while the company is organized, registered, or doing business in California. Corporations follow the minimum franchise tax and estimated-payment rules. An LLC that elects corporate tax treatment follows the corporate rules.


## Which $800 tax applies?


Tax classification Payment to check First-year rule


LLC taxed as a partnership or disregarded entity Annual LLC tax, generally paid using FTB 3522 or the matching Web Pay option The temporary first-year exemption applied to tax years beginning in 2021 through 2023. Do not assume a newly formed LLC has that exemption now.


C corporation Corporate estimated tax, using Form 100-ES or electronic payment A newly incorporated or qualified corporation generally avoids the minimum franchise tax in its first taxable year, but may still owe tax on income.


S corporation, including an LLC taxed as an S corporation Corporate estimated tax Check the corporate first-year rules and income-based tax. An S election does not eliminate California tax.


Read the FTB guidance for[LLCs](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/limited-liability-company/index.html) ,[C corporations](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/corporations/c-corporations.html) , and[S corporations](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/corporations/s-corporations.html) before choosing a payment.


## When is the California $800 tax due?


For an existing calendar-year LLC under the annual LLC tax rules, the usual payment deadline is April 15 of the current tax year. A new domestic LLC generally pays by the 15th day of the fourth month measured from its formation date. Foreign LLCs that begin doing business or register partway through a year need to check the FTB's specific first-year instructions.


For corporations subject to the minimum franchise tax, at least the minimum generally must be paid by the first estimated-tax installment date: the 15th day of the fourth month of the taxable year. A corporation may owe additional estimated tax based on income.


Do not wait until the following year's return deadline to make a current-year payment. See the[FTB's LLC guidance](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/limited-liability-company/index.html) and[Form 100-ES instructions](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/2026/2026-100-es-instructions.html) . Check holiday, disaster-relief and fiscal-year rules where relevant.


## Payment dates and return dates are different


For a calendar-year corporation, the original C corporation return deadline is generally April 15 of the following year; the S corporation deadline is generally March 15. Those are return deadlines, not the current-year minimum-tax payment deadline. Check the[FTB business due-date table](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/when-to-file/due-dates-business.html) for your classification and tax year. An extension to file does not extend the time to pay.


## What counts as doing business in California?


The FTB's[doing-business tests](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/doing-business-in-california.html) include transactions for financial gain in California, being organized or commercially domiciled there, and exceeding the applicable sales, property, or payroll tests. The thresholds change by tax year, so use the table for the year under review.


An out-of-state mailing address does not settle the question. Review where the company operates and where its staff and property sit, along with its California sales. Registration with the Secretary of State can create a filing and tax duty even when a separate doing-business test is not the reason for it.


## How to pay the tax


1. **Confirm the entity and classification.** Have the legal name, California entity number and tax year ready. Check any election notice rather than relying on the company name.
2. **Choose the payment channel.** Open the[FTB business payment page](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/payment-options.html) . Use the available electronic option or the applicable voucher.
3. **Select the correct payment type.** An annual LLC tax payment and a corporation estimated-tax payment are different. The LLC annual tax is also separate from an estimated LLC fee.
4. **Check the period before submitting.** A payment credited to the wrong year can leave the intended obligation unpaid.
5. **Save the confirmation.** Record the amount, payment date, tax year, payment type and confirmation number in your books.


If a payment already appears on your bank statement but not in the expected tax period, check the payment record with the FTB before paying again.


## Annual tax, LLC fee and SOI filing are separate


The $800 annual LLC tax is not the same as the additional LLC fee that can apply based on California income. Nor does paying the FTB satisfy the Secretary of State's Statement of Information requirement.


Use separate calendar entries for:


- Annual or estimated tax payments.
- Any additional LLC fee.
- The income tax return.
- The[California Statement of Information](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/california-SOI-guide) .


That separation helps prevent an on-time filing from hiding a missed payment.


## Common questions


### Do I owe the tax if the business has no revenue?


An inactive company can still owe the annual or minimum tax. Do not treat zero revenue, a closed bank account or an unused company as evidence that the entity has ended. Check the applicable FTB rules and complete the required cancellation or dissolution process.


### What if the company formed at the end of the year?


The[FTB corporation guidance](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/file/business/types/corporations/index.html) provides a short-year exception when the tax year lasts 15 days or less and the corporation conducts no California business during it. Both conditions matter. The[LLC filing guidance](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/forms/misc/3556.html) also describes its short-year rule. Do not treat every December formation as exempt.


### Is the first year free for a California LLC?


Do not apply the former temporary LLC exemption to a new tax year outside its stated period. Also distinguish an LLC under the annual-tax rules from an LLC that elected corporate tax treatment.


### What if I paid late?


Check the account balance and applicable[FTB penalties and interest](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/penalties-and-interest/index.html) . The standard late-payment penalty includes 5% of unpaid tax plus 0.5% for each month or part of a month, up to the stated limit. For LLCs, the FTB applies it to underpaid annual tax, fees, and other covered amounts. Corporate estimated-tax penalties follow a separate calculation. A tax payment, late-payment penalty and estimated-tax penalty are not interchangeable. Keep any relief request and the FTB's response with the payment record.


### Does paying $800 complete my California filing?


No. The payment does not replace the return, other applicable taxes or the SOI filing. Use your entity's filing requirements to close each obligation separately.
